stem: After a medication error, an interprofessional team reviews workflow, staffing, technology, communication, equipment, and the care environment to identify contributing factors and redesign the process. Which patient-safety approach does this describe?

options.A: Individual-fault review focused primarily on identifying and retraining the person who made the final error.
options.B: Failure modes and effects analysis used prospectively to predict how a process could fail before an event occurs.
options.C: A no-accountability model in which individual training, preparation, and behavior are never considered during event review.
options.D: System-focused event investigation and analysis aimed at identifying contributing system factors and developing safer, sustainable solutions.

rationale: AHRQ's CANDOR System-Focused Event Investigation and Analysis Guide describes a systems approach that examines contributing factors such as staffing, technology, equipment, environment, communication, teamwork, and task/process design so that safer and more sustainable solutions can be developed. D therefore matches the scenario. A is too narrow and reflects the individual-blame/retraining approach AHRQ warns may fail to produce sustained improvement. B describes a prospective risk-analysis method rather than retrospective investigation of an event that already occurred. C is also incorrect because AHRQ explicitly states that a systems approach is not a blame-free culture and does not eliminate individual accountability for training, preparation, and behavior.
educational_objective: Differentiate system-focused event investigation from individual-blame review and prospective FMEA by recognizing its emphasis on contributing system factors and process redesign after an adverse event or near miss.
source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)
source_document_title: CANDOR — System-Focused Event Investigation and Analysis Guide
source_version_date: AHRQ CANDOR current module; live page rechecked 2026-08-17
source_locator: Introduction; A Systems Approach; In-depth Event Investigation and Analysis — questions covering staffing, technology, equipment, physical environment, supervision, teamwork, communication, and task/process factors; Solutions Meeting
source_claim_supported: AHRQ's system-focused event investigation seeks contributing system factors rather than reflexive individual blame and examines organization/staffing, technology, equipment, environment, communication, teamwork, and task/process design to develop sustainable safety solutions; the approach retains appropriate individual accountability.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8/PDF p.12: Acknowledge and document practice errors and near misses; Report, intervene and/or escalate unsafe practice of staff; Participate in client safety improvement activities
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — systems-based analysis of safety events
correction_summary: Converted the original action-based alternatives into a true approach-identification item. Kept the AHRQ system-focused construct, added a plausible prospective FMEA contrast, explicitly excluded the false idea that systems analysis eliminates individual accountability, and reduced difficulty from hard to moderate.
